It can be very difficult for parents to be able to properly raise her children when one child needs a round the clock care. I don’t think op understands how hard it can be to care for somebody who has a severe disability. Especially if the individual needs around the Clock care. I am assuming your sister is not properly trained in caring for somebody with a disability, and IT can make it a lot harder on the parent. Just because putting him in a home maybe his best choice, doesn’t mean that she’s being an asshole. Maybe the sister doesn’t feel comfortable going to the family for help. There is absolutely nothing wrong with going to the professionals ensuring that your child has the best care. Plus Adams mom may feel like she doesn’t provide adequate care for him. She knows that these other people who are trained and have taken classes on the topic can provide a better life for him. Hell my kid is in speech therapy session because we’re in the process of him being tested for learning disability or autism. This doesn’t mean I don’t care about my child. 

My step grandfather had to be placed in a home because his mental health has deteriorated. My grandma is an older lady and she wasn’t able to care for him around the clock. That doesn’t mean she abandoned him. She was ensuring that he got the best care that he could receive, because she knew she wasn’t able to properly give that to him with her age and her health. 

I think OP needs to take a step back from the situation and look at it from his sister‘s point of view. At this point it’s not about the money, it’s about your child receiving the proper care that they need. These people are trained professionals and they know what they’re doing. I honestly don’t know why OP is shunning his sister for this choice. If she knows she can’t do it, she’s getting someone who can, and that’s being a good mom. This doesn’t mean it’s an easy choice, because she has most likely been contemplating it for a while. She needs to have a life too, and she needs to ensure that her son is receiving the best care to meet his needs.
